name: Dusty wine
lede: Dusty wine renders Murasakitobi (紫鳶), a traditional Japanese name meaning "purple kite", after the plumage of the black kite with a purple cast added.

sections.title: Named for a bird's plumage
sections.body:
Our color library gives the source as 紫鳶 (Murasakitobi) [1]. Tobi is the black kite, a bird of prey whose brown plumage long named a whole family of browns in Japanese dyeing; murasaki, purple, marks this one as the reddish-purple member of that family [1]. No first-recorded date survives in our sources, so when the name entered use is undocumented here [1]. The library's own near-duplicate note pairs this hue with "Reddish wine tone," at a color distance of just 2.4, under the Dusty mahogany entry [1].

The nearest named color in our graph is [[rubient]], at a color distance (ΔE2000) of 4.2, a more vivid shade; [[black-red]] sits 4.4 away and reads darker [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this dark red-brown in 307 of 23,781 paintings, about 1.3 percent, as photographed [3]. It peaks in the 1580s (7 of 166 paintings from that decade) and is especially strong in portraiture, led by Gustave Caillebotte at more than ten times the overall rate, with Caravaggio and Diego Velázquez not far behind [3]. By country, Spain holds the largest share, followed by Germany and Italy [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings; the match is computed, not a pigment identification [3].
